name: com.cromanion/cromanion
title: Cromanion
description: Read live visits with a developer key, or raise conversion with no human by proving the domain.

tools.name: cromanion_open_claim
tools.description: Start here, and you need nothing to do it — no API key, no human. This call takes no credential and creates NOTHING: no account, no key, no charge. It returns a challenge to publish on the site you manage (a file, a meta tag or a DNS record — whichever your hosting lets you write) and the secret you will authenticate with once the proof is read. That proof is the whole trust model: we cannot take your word for an email address, but we can check what you control. Store the secret; it is shown once. Refuses if the address already has an account, because controlling a site does not prove controlling a mailbox.

email.description: Your human's email. It becomes the account's login.

siteUrl.description: The public URL of the site to optimize, e.g. https://example.com.

agent.description: Optional: what you call yourself, for support and audit.

tools.name: cromanion_verify_claim
tools.description: Redeem a claim once you have published one of its three proofs (a /.well-known file, a <meta> tag, or a DNS TXT record). On success it creates the account and the site and returns the tracking snippet to install. Idempotent — safe to retry. Requires the claim secret as a bearer token.

tools.name: cromanion_site_status
tools.description: Check the site you provisioned: whether the tag is actually live (a beacon received from your own domain, not merely a snippet handed to you), how the crawl is going, and the plan. Poll this after installing the snippet. Requires the claim secret as a bearer token.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

tools.name: cromanion_install_check
tools.description: Why the tag is not firing. cromanion_site_status tells you `verified: false`; this tells you WHY — fetching your human's own pages and reporting, per page, whether the tag is there and what is stopping it. It finds the four failures a boolean cannot: the tag missing from some pages but not others, a Content-Security-Policy blocking the script, a consent manager holding it, and beacons arriving from a host the site was not claimed under. Each comes back with the fix. Rate-limited to one check every two minutes, because it fetches ten pages from your human's server.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

tools.name: cromanion_upgrade_link
tools.description: Get a Stripe Checkout link for a paid plan (pro or growth). Returns a URL and nothing else — YOU do not pay and cannot: give the link to your human, who enters their own card. The site works on the free plan meanwhile. Requires the claim secret as a bearer token.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

plan.description: Which paid plan the link should check out: pro or growth. The site keeps working on free until your human completes it.

tools.name: cromanion_errors
tools.description: Every refusal this server can return, and what to do about each. Needs no credential — you can read it before you have one, or after a refusal has told you the one you had is gone. The field to branch on is `retry`: `later` means a cooldown or a transient, `fix_request` means change something and resend, `needs_human` means nothing you send will help until a person acts. Read it once and stop guessing whether a 409 is worth retrying.

tools.name: cromanion_grants
tools.description: List what your human has allowed this agent to do, and what they have not. Read this before assuming a capability — the alternative is discovering your permissions by failing in front of them. You cannot change these yourself; only your human can, in their console.

tools.name: cromanion_pending
tools.description: Everything on this site that is waiting for a decision: page rewrites the agent wants to make, rules it distilled from real sessions, conversions it spotted but has never counted, and pages your traffic found that the crawl missed. This is the client's actual job in the console, in one call. Rule on an item with cromanion_decide.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

tools.name: cromanion_config
tools.description: Everything IN FORCE on this site: the conversions that count, the facts you may state and the ones forbidden, which surfaces are enabled, the brand, and every distilled rule WITH its status. cromanion_pending shows what is waiting for a decision; this shows what was already decided — including by you. Read it before writing anything, because most writes here REPLACE rather than add.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

tools.name: cromanion_decide
tools.description: Rule on one thing from cromanion_pending: pass its `kind` and `id` back unchanged with a decision. `approve` / `reject` for everything; `pause` additionally for a playbook rule. Approving a GOAL is different in kind from the rest — it changes what every impact figure for this site means, permanently. You cannot edit rule text here, only rule on it.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

kind.description: Which queue the item came from. Copy it back from cromanion_pending unchanged.

id.description: The item's id, exactly as cromanion_pending returned it. Ids are not shared across kinds.

decision.description: A status and nothing else — rule TEXT is edited by cromanion_set_playbook. `pause` applies only to a playbook_rule.

all.description: Rule on every discovered page at once, ignoring `id`. observed_path only — the other kinds are decided one at a time, as in the console.

tools.name: cromanion_set_playbook
tools.description: Reword a distilled rule, or ask for a fresh distillation. Rules are what the agent learned from real sessions; cromanion_decide approves or pauses them, and this changes what they SAY. Send a ruleId with condition and/or recommendedAction to reword one — ids come from cromanion_config, which also shows rules you have already approved or paused. Send redistill: true instead to distil new rules from recent sessions; they arrive as `proposed` for you to rule on. Rate-limited to one distillation an hour. Needs the decisions permission.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

ruleId.description: The rule to reword, from cromanion_config.

condition.description: When the rule applies, in plain words. Omit to leave it.

recommendedAction.description: What the agent should do when it applies. Omit to leave it.

redistill.description: Ignore ruleId and distil fresh rules from recent sessions instead.

tools.name: cromanion_ask_human
tools.description: Ask your human for something only they can do, in a place they will actually see it. Every other refusal here ends with YOU reading it — a permission they did not grant, a payment you cannot make, a mode you may not set — and from their side you simply went quiet. This puts one request on their notifications screen, attributed to you. Nothing replies here: they act in their console, and you find out by reading cromanion_grants or cromanion_config again. One request an hour, and a second from you replaces the first rather than stacking.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

title.description: What you need, in a line they can read at a glance. Up to 90 characters.

body.description: Why you need it and what it unblocks, in a sentence or two. Up to 400 characters.

tools.name: cromanion_mark_read
tools.description: Mark notifications read once you have passed them on to your human. cromanion_pending returns the unread ones and nothing cleared them, so the queue grew for ever and you re-read the same items on every poll. Send a notificationId for one, or nothing to clear them all. Needs the decisions permission.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

notificationId.description: One notification, by the id cromanion_pending returned. Omit to mark every unread one read.

tools.name: cromanion_impact
tools.description: What the agent has actually changed: visitors who saw it versus the 10% held back as a control. Read `liftStatus` before reporting anything — `learn` means nothing has been shown yet and `insufficient` means the arms are too small to tell signal from noise. Neither is 'no lift'.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

tools.name: cromanion_visits
tools.description: List your human's recent visits — each with its pages, how it ended, what Cromanion's agent showed or held back, the doubts it read, and the start of the visit's story. Filter by page, outcome, doubt, device, channel and more; page through with `next`. Needs the visits permission, which only your human can give in their console. Everything under `reading` is Cromanion's interpretation, not something the visitor said — report it that way. A visit is readable in full about 30 minutes after the visitor leaves; for who is on the site right now use cromanion_live. The control group is never read, so a doubt filter contains no control visits. Shares a budget of 60 calls an hour with cromanion_visit; every call is on your human's record before it runs. Identifiers in paths are masked (`:id`, `:token`), so products addressed by a number or a code are indistinguishable to a page filter.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

since.description: ISO date. Visits that STARTED at or after it. Default: 24 hours ago. At most 30 days back.

until.description: ISO date. Visits that started before it. Default: now.

page.description: Visits that viewed this path — exact, or a prefix ending in `*` (`/products/*`). Pages your human excluded are refused, not answered with zero.

outcome.description: `left` = ended without your human's conversion. Default `any`.

objection.description: Visits where the model read this doubt at least once. A reading, not a fact.

agentAction.description: Visits where the agent's intervention was seen, sent, held back, or where the site was still learning. Default `any`.

device.description: The device the visit arrived on.

channel.description: How the visit was acquired — a closed label, never a campaign name.

visitor.description: First visit, or a returning visitor (a coarse, cookieless reading).

population.description: People (default), AI shopping agents, or both. Crawlers and scripts are never listed.

tools.name: cromanion_visit
tools.description: One visit in full: the story of each page load, every moment Cromanion's agent looked at the visitor and what it decided, what the visitor actually saw, and the doubts it read. Pass the `visitId` from cromanion_visits, or a `sessionId` from cromanion_live once that visitor has left. Needs the visits permission. Readings sit under `reading`; a moment at or after the conversion carries `observed` instead, because the conversion is a fact. `shown.seen` is what the visitor's browser confirmed, not what was sent. Same 60-an-hour budget as cromanion_visits.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

sessionId.description: Instead of visitId: any session of the visit, e.g. one seen in cromanion_live.

tools.name: cromanion_live
tools.description: Who is on your human's site right now: each visitor's pages so far, what the agent showed them, and its current reading of them. Paid plans only (Pro and up) — on Free it is refused with the way to upgrade. Needs the visits permission. Poll at most once a minute; this has its own budget, separate from the history tools. Bots are judged when a visit ends, so a robot not yet recognised can appear here as a person.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

population.description: People (default), AI shopping agents, or both.

tools.name: get_visit
tools.description: For a Live Visit Feed site: one visit's last feed event, read from the edge while the visit is in progress and from the store after it ends. Pass the `visit_id` a feed event, list_live_visits or list_agent_visits carries. It needs an API key from the developer console, which holds the visits permission, and the feed turned on for the site; a conversion site's credential is refused with not_feed_site. A visit in progress is readable from the moment it opens its feed, and the answer says `live: true`: the event was read from the edge, which still holds the visit. Otherwise the stored event is returned, with `live: false`. An event is stored at an exit signal, at a conversion and when the visit ends. So if the edge cannot be reached, a visit in progress shows a stored event that can be minutes old, or answers not_found when none was stored yet. `as_of` says when the event was built. A very long narrative keeps its last 2,000 characters. `preview_score` is a score trained on purchases, not on the site's goals, and is null unless the site turned scoring on. On a site that has its own model, `interest` is that model's score for the visit, 0 to 1, with `model` naming the model, under the same consent, and `preview_score` is null; `interest` and `model` are null otherwise. `control_group: true` marks the permanent holdout: Cromanion never acts on those visits, and the feed still describes them. A visit later judged a bot keeps the event it was sent. 60 calls an hour per key, shared with get_page_attention and list_agent_visits; every call is on the developer's record before it runs.

visit_id.description: The `vis_…` id from a feed event, from list_live_visits or from list_agent_visits.

tools.name: list_live_visits
tools.description: For a Live Visit Feed site: the visits on the site right now, from the live board. Each carries its `visit_id`, when it started and was last seen, and the moment, elapsed time and score of its last feed event. A visit is listed once it opened a feed: a real gesture or a conversion, never a bounce, a crawler or a driven browser. It needs an API key from the developer console and the feed turned on for the site; a conversion site's credential is refused with not_feed_site. `interest` is the site's own model's score, 0 to 1, with `model` naming the model; both are null until the site has one. `preview_score` is a score trained on purchases, not on the site's goals; it is null on a site that has its own model. All three are null unless the site turned scoring on. `control_group: true` marks the permanent holdout: Cromanion never acts on those visits, and the feed still describes them. An ended visit stays listed for ten minutes. Six calls a minute per key, a budget of its own; every call is on the developer's record before it runs. Pass a `visit_id` to get_visit for the visit's whole last event.

tools.name: get_page_attention
tools.description: For a Live Visit Feed site: which sections of one page its visitors study, added up from the stored feed events. Pass `page`, one page's path. Read the limit first: Cromanion stores one feed event per visit, the last one, and its attention table covers one page, the page the visit was on at that event. So the figures come from the visits whose last feed event was on this page. A visit that read the page and then went to another one is not counted, and the figures do not describe everyone who saw the page. Per section: the visits whose event lists it, the total and the median seconds it was on screen, the visits per engagement grade (studied, read, skimmed) and the returns. Under 30 visits the answer gives the count, says `enough: false` and withholds the sections. `visitor_kind` is `human` (the default) or `ai_agent`; the two are never added together. The window is the last 7 days unless you pass `since` and `until`, at most 30 days back, read on the visit's start. A visit judged a bot when it ended, a visit marked as the site's own, and a visit with no stored feed event (a bounce, or a visit made while the feed was off) are not counted. `page` is matched as the events write it: without query or trailing slash, with an email or a token segment replaced, a numeric id kept; no wildcard. It needs an API key from the developer console and the feed turned on for the site; a conversion site's credential is refused with not_feed_site. 60 calls an hour per key, shared with get_visit and list_agent_visits; every call is on the developer's record before it runs.

page.description: One page's path, starting with `/`, e.g. /products/the-edge. No host. Matched exactly: no character is a wildcard.

since.description: ISO date. Default: 7 days before `until`. At most 30 days back.

visitor_kind.description: People (default) or AI agents. Never both in one answer.

tools.name: list_agent_visits
tools.description: For a Live Visit Feed site: the AI agents that visited, newest first, each with the pages it saw and the story of its visit. A visit is listed when its visitor was an AI agent (an agentic browser or an AI fetcher: `visitor.kind` `ai_agent`, as in a feed event) and the visit stored a feed event. Each row: `visit_id`, `started_at`, `as_of` and `ended` (when the stored event was built, and whether it is the visit's last), `visitor.ai_agent` with `vendor` and `verification`, `pages`, `converted`, `reached_checkout` when it was recorded, and `narrative`. `verification` says how the agent's identity was proven. `web_bot_auth`: it signed its requests, and the signature was checked against the key published at its own origin. `cloudflare_verified_bot`: Cloudflare verified it as an AI bot, which proves the kind of bot and not who runs it. `null`: nothing was proven, and the visit is called an agent's on its user-agent's word alone. `vendor` is the operator, or `other` when it could not be attributed. Never listed: a crawler, a browser driven by a script, a visit judged a bot when it ended, a visit marked as the site's own. Not listed either: an agent's visit that stored no feed event, because it opened no feed (a page load with no gesture and no conversion) or the feed was off; and an agent that names itself nowhere is recorded as a person. So the list is a floor on agent traffic, not its total. `pages` is the stored page list: without query or trailing slash, a numeric id written `:id`, an email or a token replaced. `converted` is an observed goal or a confirmed purchase. The window is the last 7 days unless you pass `since` and `until`, at most 30 days back, read on the visit's start. `limit` is 1 to 50, default 20; pass `next` back as `cursor` for older visits. Pass a `visit_id` to get_visit for the visit's whole last event. It needs an API key from the developer console and the feed turned on for the site; a conversion site's credential is refused with not_feed_site. 60 calls an hour per key, shared with get_visit and get_page_attention; every call is on the developer's record before it runs.

since.description: ISO date. Default: 7 days before `until`. At most 30 days back.

cursor.description: The `next` of the previous page. It carries its own window.

tools.name: cromanion_set_mode
tools.description: Switch the agent on. `learn` watches and shows visitors nothing; `act` lets it intervene in your human's name. `customizeMode` is a separate axis for rewriting their own page copy: `off`, `shadow` (propose only) or `live`. Needs the activation permission.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

mode.description: `learn` watches and shows visitors nothing; `act` lets the agent intervene in your human's name. Omit to leave it as it is.

customizeMode.description: Rewriting your human's own page copy, a separate axis from `mode`: `off`, `shadow` (propose only, nothing shown) or `live`. Omit to leave it as it is.

tools.name: cromanion_add_goal
tools.description: Define a conversion to count, or change one you already defined. This is not one more setting: it is the numerator of every impact figure your human will read, so a goal that fires on every pageview makes the agent look brilliant and tells them nothing. Send `type` and `value` to create — idempotent, the same matcher twice creates one goal. Send `goalId` instead to rename, reprioritise or price an existing one, or with `remove: true` to stop counting it. Needs the goals permission.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

type.description: Matcher: css_click, form_submit, page_view, mailto, tel, outbound, scroll_depth, dwell, custom_event.

value.description: What the matcher matches — a selector, a path, a percentage, seconds.

label.description: What your human will call it. Defaults to something readable.

dollarValue.description: Optional worth of one conversion, for revenue figures.

goalId.description: Change an EXISTING goal instead of creating one. Ids come from cromanion_config. With `remove: true` it stops counting that conversion; otherwise it applies the label, priority or dollarValue you send.

remove.description: With goalId: stop counting that conversion. Nothing already measured is rewritten.

priority.description: With goalId: 1 is the primary goal, ascending. Rejected rather than clamped if out of range.

tools.name: cromanion_crawl
tools.description: Re-read the site, and name the pages that matter most so they are read first. You know this site's structure better than its owner does — seeding it is the cheapest real improvement to what the agent understands. Rate-limited: one crawl per 30 minutes. Needs the site-config permission.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

priorityUrls.description: Up to 10 paths or URLs to read first, e.g. ["/pricing", "/checkout"]. Anything unusable is handed back rather than dropped.

tools.name: cromanion_add_site
tools.description: Add another of your human's sites to their account, on a plan that allows more than one. Reaching a site they already own needs no proof — they added it. CREATING one does: nothing about holding a credential for one domain says anything about another, so publish this claim's challenge on the new domain first, the same three ways that proved the first. Refused while this credential is limited to specific sites, which is how one you provisioned yourself starts (the site it proved): your human widens it in the console — use cromanion_ask_human. Needs the site-config permission.

siteUrl.description: The public https URL of the site to add, e.g. https://second-shop.com.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

tools.name: cromanion_claim_domain
tools.description: Claim another host for this site so its traffic counts, or give one up with `remove: true`. A DIFFERENT registrable domain must be proven on its own — publish this claim's challenge there too, then call again. Subdomains need no call at all: a claimed domain already covers them. Needs the site-config permission.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

remove.description: Give the host up instead. Needs no proof — it only narrows what we listen to.

tools.name: cromanion_set_voice
tools.description: Write the facts the agent may state to visitors, and the things it must never say. Plain sentences, one idea per line; start a line with 'never' to forbid something. Anything you write that your human's own pages do not already state is attributed to THEM as the source — so write only what they have told you is true. Every rule is checked against your own text and the site's vocabulary, and anything ungrounded is silently dropped: read the returned `lines` to see what actually survived. Your human sees each line attributed to you. Needs the voice permission.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

text.description: The whole guidance, replacing what is there. An empty string clears it.

tools.name: cromanion_set_surfaces
tools.description: Choose where the agent may speak and what those places look like: which layout surfaces are enabled, whether the exit modal is allowed, custom CSS, and per-surface HTML. Markup and CSS are re-checked against an allowlist on every visitor — anything that could run, or fetch a remote resource, is silently removed, so compare what comes back with what you sent. Needs the surfaces permission.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

enabled.description: Surfaces the agent may use: inline_hint, card, sticky_bar, bottom_sheet, inline_block, cta_tooltip.

allowModal.description: Allow the page-blocking exit modal. Off by default.

customCss.description: CSS applied inside the intervention's shadow root. An empty string clears it.

templates.description: Per-surface HTML, keyed by surface. Use {{message}}, {{cta_label}} and {{cta_url}} as placeholders.

tools.name: cromanion_set_holdout
tools.description: Set the share of visitors held back from the agent so its effect stays measurable (0.05–0.5). Changing it splits the measurement window: periods either side are compared separately and never pooled. Needs the measurement permission.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

tools.name: cromanion_set_exclusions
tools.description: Put an excluded device back into the measurement. Your human can mark their own devices as "not a real visitor" so their browsing does not count; this removes one of those marks, by the label they gave it. You cannot ADD an exclusion — that names the caller's own browser, which you do not have. Needs the measurement permission.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

label.description: The label your human gave the device, as cromanion_config lists it. An ambiguous label is refused rather than guessed at.

tools.name: cromanion_set_brand
tools.description: Adjust the palette, fonts and button styling the agent paints its surfaces with. The crawl guesses these from a stylesheet; you probably know the real tokens. Cosmetic only — it changes how the agent looks, never what it may say. Needs the brand permission.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

colors.description: Hex per role, e.g. {"primary":"#1a1a2e"}. Roles come from cromanion_site_status.

headingFont.description: CSS font-family stack for headings, e.g. "Inter, sans-serif".

bodyFont.description: CSS font-family stack for body text, e.g. "Inter, sans-serif".

tools.name: cromanion_set_lead_destination
tools.description: Set where captured leads are delivered: an https webhook, a connected HubSpot portal, or off. Note before you use it: this is the one change that leaves no other trace — forms keep working and visitors keep being thanked while the addresses go somewhere new — so every change emails your human and appears on their notifications screen. Needs the integrations permission.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.

kind.description: Where leads go: `webhook` posts them to your `target` URL, `hubspot` to the connected portal, `off` stops delivery while forms keep working.

target.description: The https webhook URL. Not needed for hubspot or off.

tools.name: cromanion_disconnect_hubspot
tools.description: Sever the account's HubSpot connection. The other half of cromanion_set_lead_destination's `hubspot` option: you can point leads at a CRM, so you can take them back out. Refused while any site on the account still delivers there — change those destinations first, or the forms would keep working while every lead failed delivery. Reconnecting is NOT a tool: it is an OAuth consent screen only your human can click, so treat this as one-way and say so before you call it. Needs the integrations permission.

siteId.description: Which site this call is about. Only needed when your credential covers more than one — cromanion_grants lists them and says whether it is required. Omitting it with several is refused rather than guessed at.
